assumptions: The package snapshot is immutable, completely selected, and syntax-valid.
Protocol versions and the specification digest are the reviewed Gantry v1 values.
The Boolean model abstracts finite implementation judgments and is not an enumeration of all source programs.
Capture-avoiding substitution, unification, coherence, and lowering are justified by the written argument and property evidence rather than by the finite Boolean search.

trait Label { pure fn label(self) -> String; } struct Envelope<T> { value: T } impl<T> Label for Envelope<T> { pure fn label(self) -> String { "generic" } } impl Label for Envelope<String> { pure fn label(self) -> String { "specific" } } fn main() {}

trait First<T> { pure fn label(self) -> String; } trait Second<T> { pure fn second(self) -> String; } struct Item {} struct Envelope<T> { value: T } impl<T> First<T> for Envelope<T> where T: Second<Envelope<T>> { pure fn label(self) -> String { "first" } } impl<T> Second<T> for Item where T: First<Item> { pure fn second(self) -> String { "second" } } fn main(value: Envelope<Item>) -> String { First::<Item>::label(value) }

metamorphic_cases.right: trait Label { pure fn label(self) -> String; } struct First {} struct Second {} impl Label for Second { pure fn label(self) -> String { "second" } } impl Label for First { pure fn label(self) -> String { "first" } } fn main() {}

metamorphic_cases.left: trait First { pure fn first(self); } trait Second { pure fn second(self); } struct Item {} impl First for Item { pure fn first(self) {} } impl Second for Item { pure fn second(self) {} } fn inspect<T>(value: T) where T: First, T: Second { value.first(); value.second(); } fn main(value: Item) { inspect(value); }
